chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib and Yaqoub Al Sarraj, altogether, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'O people! The transgressor will be guiding his companions to the Fire, and that the first one who transgressed against Allah was Anaaq, daughter of Adam. Thus, the first one whom Allah killed was Anaaq; and when sitting she would occupy one acre. And she had twenty fingers, in every finger there being two nails similar to a scythe. So Allah made a lion like the elephant, and a wolf like the camel, and an eagle like the mule to kill her. So they killed her, and Allah has killed the tyrants upon the best of their states, and (when they were) as safe as they could have been.'
ai.seo_question: Who was the first person to transgress against Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi links the cosmic principle of al-baghy (transgression/extravagance) to the first human homicide, identifying Cain (Qabil) as the first to transgress against God by killing Abel. It illustrates the theological concept that divine punishment often strikes tyrants at the peak of their security, a theme reinforced by the detailed description of Anaaq’s unique physical traits and her death by God-sent beasts.
